1. **PR description/diff mismatch (blocking)** — The PR title/body describe fixing `mkShellArgs.packages` being dropped in `nix/modules/project/devshell.nix`, with changes to `devshell.nix`, `test/simple/flake.nix`, and `doc/devshell.md`. The actual diff touches none of those files — it only adds `default = lib.id;` to the unrelated `custom` cabal setting in `nix/modules/project/settings/all.nix`. This has to be resolved before review can even proceed: either the wrong diff/branch was attached, or the description is stale/hallucinated. Fix: re-generate the PR from the correct branch so the diff matches the stated intent, or rewrite the description to describe what's actually being changed.

2. **`nix/modules/project/settings/all.nix` — `default = lib.id` doesn't address a "defined multiple times" error.** The title claims this fixes `custom` "expected to be unique," which in the NixOS module system is the error you get when an option whose type has no merge function (here `types.functionTo types.package`) receives definitions from more than one module. Adding a `default` only removes the requirement that the option be set at all — it does nothing for the case where two modules both *do* set `custom`, which is presumably the actual trigger for the uniqueness error. Fix: identify the actual code path producing the "unique" error (likely in `mkCabalSettingOptions`/how per-package settings are merged across modules), and address the merge behavior directly (e.g. via `mkMerge`/priorities, or composing multiple `custom` functions) rather than just supplying a default.

3. **No regression test for the claimed fix.** The only test added per the description targets `mkShellArgs.packages` in `devshell.nix`, which isn't part of this diff at all. There's no test demonstrating the original "`custom` expected to be unique" error and verifying it's gone after this change. Fix: add a minimal reproduction (two modules/overrides both defining `custom` for the same package, or whatever reproduces the original error) to `test/` and confirm it now evaluates successfully.

4. **Unreviewed semantic change to `custom`'s "unset" behavior.** Making `custom` default to `lib.id` changes it from "must be explicitly provided wherever settings application assumes a value" to "always has a value, silently a no-op when unset." Need to confirm how `custom`'s `impl` is invoked in `lib.mkCabalSettingOptions`/the settings pipeline — if that code special-cased "not defined" (e.g. via `options.custom.isDefined` or similar) to skip applying it, this change may alter behavior for existing configs that never set `custom`. Fix: trace the actual application site and confirm `lib.id` composes correctly with however other settings are piped, and document the new default in the option's `description`.
